title: Windowed ingest loss causing undercount during batched fallback routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported month-to-month billing deltas where billed token usage was lower than expected for heavy bursty workloads. Investigation shows a class of requests that experienced a routing fallback mid-batch (hot-to-cold model variant or cross-region fallback) were sometimes dropped from the final metering window, causing persistent undercounting for those tenants across Hosted, Dedicated, and older Private runtimes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a synthetic client that emits 400-1600 token requests in rapid succession with request concurrency > 30 and route policy set to allow model-variant fallback (cost-tier fallback enabled).
2) Configure serving pool to evict a worker during a batch window (simulate preemption/scale-down) or force a fallback policy to a cheaper variant mid-request via routing toggle.

3) Observe that one or more requests in the final preemption window are acknowledged to the client but the ingestion pipeline never persisted their token counts to the billing rollup due to an orphaned batch context.
4) Query the token-aggregation service for the tenant time-window and compare streaming logs vs final ledger entries to see missing deltas.
observations: Missing increments all correlate to requests that were in-flight when a routing decision changed (host->dedicated fallback or variant downgrade).
Batch context object lifecycle contains a short path where 'finalize_and_emit' is skipped if routing returns non-local downstream task ids.
Only manifests for sequences using continuous batching (not single-request fastpath) and older private runtime < 1.22; hosted and dedicated show occurrences during autoscale preemption windows.
Affected customers: FinGov Analytics (large bursty evaluation jobs) and ShopSalad (PLG spike with retry storm).
root_cause: A race between the batching finalizer and the fallback-routing handoff. When a batch is split and individual requests are reassigned to a fallback variant mid-window, the batch finalizer kernel unhooks the in-flight batch context before persisting per-tenant deltas. This path lacked idempotent emit semantics (no durable commit) and the retry/ack logic assumed downstream persistence which didn't occur for cross-variant handoffs.
mitigation: hotfix: ensure the batch finalizer persists per-request token delta to the durable ledger before any routing handoff returns success to the client (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1484).
deploy immediate config: disable cross-variant fallback in the 1-hour window for heavy-concurrency tenants (config rollout applied to hosted control plane).
backfill: run ledger reingest using streaming snapshots for affected tenant windows (script: confluence.redwood.io/Backfill-Recipes#75555).
work_completed: Added atomic commit in batch finalizer and end-to-end tests (unit+integration).
Merged PR github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1484 and deployed hotfix to hosted canary (canary region: us-west-2).
Ran backfill job for FinGov Analytics covering 2026-02-08 to 2026-03-02; results reconciled to expected delta and credit issued.
Customer comms: sent targeted incident update to ShopSalad and FinGov; billing credits proposal approved by finance (ticket FIN-2026-183).
next_steps: 1) Complete private runtime patch release 1.22.2 and coordinate with channel partners for staged upgrades (target: 2026-03-18).
2) Add end-to-end synthetic workload in perf lab to breakpoint routing handoffs and assert ledger durability (owner: Marco Ruiz).
3) Run a 30-day audit across hosted and dedicated tenants to detect silent undercounts (owner: Billing Squad).
4) Postmortem document and run a cross-team blameless review next week; include recommended SLO for metering durability.
